best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Healing% boost and an most importantly a 15% ATK% boost for the entire team, lasting 30 seconds whenever you heal yourself or any of your allies. This bonus can be triggered by character abilities and weapon effects, is easy to keep active 100% of the time and is a big help for all party members.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Grants 10% Energy Regen on cast, making it possible to run a Spectro DMG 3-cost on Shorekeeper using 4-star weapons while still reaching the 230% Energy Regen requirement Shorekeeper must meet, which can boost her personal damage a good amount. On top of this, the Echo also grants the entire team a 10% boost to ATK for 20 seconds and deals damage based on the wearers HP, so it will slightly boost both Shorekeeper's and the whole team's damage contribution, making it her best choice generally.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Niche set for Shorekeeper in Jingran teams that don't feature a natural Shielld applier. Ran in favour of Rejuvenating Glow since this set grants a base 20% ATK permanently to all characters in the team as long as the healer can apply Healing constantly off-field, something Shorekeeper is capable of. 5% better than Rejuvenating Glow's 15% ATK and less clunky to use thanks to having a Summon Echo instead of a Transform one on Rejuvenating Glow (which would be Stonewall Bracer).

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Grants a Shield when summoned on cast, provides Jingran with a massive Fusion DMG Bonus boost if a Shielding teammate like Iuno isn't there to generate Shields without the need for this Echo.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Shorekeeper's Signature is her best weapon but not by a big difference compared to Variation. It does provide a 14% team-wide ATK boost when casting Shorekeeper's skill and provides an extra Concerto boost when casting Ultimate. Additionally, it increases Energy Regen by a massive amount, making reaching Shorekeeper's 230% requirement easy. However, due to providing lower amounts of Concerto than an R5 Variation, its competition is fierce as this weapon makes Shorekeeper's opening rotation noticeably slower.

weapon_base_info.effect_description: Increase HP by {0}. Restore {1} Concerto Energy when casting Resonance Liberation. This effect can be triggered 1 time(s) every 20s. When casting Resonance Skill that heals, increase nearby party members' ATK by {2} for 30s. Effects of the same name cannot be stacked.

best_weapons.commentary_details: The best 4-star weapon in the game for many players, Variation provides a simple, yet massive Concerto boost when casting Skill on top of a massive amount of Energy Regen. This weapon speeds up Shorekeeper's rotation significantly and makes her rotations quick and smooth, making it one of the best choices very close to her Signature even at R1.

weapon_base_info.effect_description: When Resonance Skill is released, restores Concerto Energy by {0}. This effect can be triggered 1 time every 20s.

best_weapons.commentary_details: The best option for Shorekeeper that doesn't require any gacha. Provides a big amount of Energy Regen and a small ATK% boost when casting Skill, acquired for free via crafting.

weapon_base_info.effect_description: When Resonance Skill is released, if the Resonator's HP is below 60%, restores their HP by {0}. This effect can be triggered 1 time(s) every 8s; if the Resonator's HP is above 60%, increases ATK by {1}, lasting for 10s.

best_weapons.commentary_details: More healing-focused option for Shorekeeper which is also given for free via an Exploration quest in Rinascita. Provides the same amount of Energy Regen as the above options, but has the added pro of increasing Healing Bonus by 16% for 15s when casting Ultimate. Better than Rectifier#25 if the player desires more healing on the team, but it is not a necessity.

weapon_base_info.effect_description: Casting Resonance Liberation increases the Resonator's Healing Bonus by {0} for 15s.

cons: Has no unique niche that she partakes in. Shorekeeper is only ever a generalist, never a specialized Support like Mornye or Chisa, who have specific categories of characters they excel with;

Her CRIT Rate buff has gotten lower value with time as more characters can naturally reach 100% CRIT Rate by themselves. This and her lack of interaction with specialized mechanics means a lot of Shorekeeper's strength is heavily at the mercy of Kuro's kit design for future damage dealers;
Awkward and lengthy rotations without a Concerto weapon available.
pros: Unique buffs to CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG. One of the strongest generalist Supports;
Fully quickswap-friendly (so long as you account for the scaling of her Intro, which isn't a major drawback);
Fast rotation, accessible weapon options, and easy to invest into, following the trend of other low-damaging general Supports;
The only limited character from the 1.x versions that stood the test of time, and is still receiving new teams where she is best in slot to this day occasionally.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Shorekeeper is a 5-star Spectro Rectifier generalist Support and healer character. She shares a similar role to Verina and can similarly fit in almost any team composition. Her unique aspect is her ability to buff allies' CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG, which usually allows her to outperform Verina in the raw damage multiplication department. Now let's dive into her kit.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
paragraphs: Shorekeeper's most important mechanic is her Stellarealm. It is summoned by casting her Ultimate, and is upgraded each time one of your characters casts their Intro, up to 2 times to max its effects. It lasts 30s at S0 and has the following effects on all allies within its range:
Outer Stellarealm (Baseline) - Coloured blue, it continuously heals all allies once every 3 seconds;
Inner Stellarealm (After 1 Intro) - Coloured purple, it increases CRIT Rate according to Shorekeeper's Energy Regen (max 12.5% at 250% Energy Regen);
Supernal Stellarealm (After 2 Intro) - Coloured gold, it increases CRIT DMG according to Shorekeeper's Energy Regen (max 25% at 250% Energy Regen).

These effects are intended to scale well with Hypercarry damage dealers: the max ramp-up will only be achieved once Shorekeeper and another character on the team have finished their rotations, so it's intended for you to play Shorekeeper in a composition with another single-target buffer (Hybrid) and a main damage dealer (DPS). She isn't limited to these types of compositions, but they definitely tend to be her best use cases.

Her other key supportive ability is her Outro, which grants the entire party a 15% Damage Amplification buff for 30 seconds. It also provides up to 5 free Perfect Dodges that you can trigger by dodging after being interrupted.

sections.heading: Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Since the two abilities we already detailed form the core of her kit and are the focus of her rotation, we can form a simple rotational idea:
Generate as much as Concerto Energy as fast as possible,
Summon the Stellarealm and then immediately perform her Outro triggering another character's Intro to upgrade the realm immediately and apply Shorekeeper's Outro buff,
After which you only require 1 more Intro to fully upgrade the realm.

To do this, she has a few tools she can use. Notably, her Forte gauge allows her to cast a special Forte Heavy Attack that generates a good chunk of Concerto. It can be built up by using Basic Attacks. Forte can also be consumed via a Mid-Air Attack, but this tends to be slow and less commonly used.

Each Basic Attack generates 1 Forte except for the Basic Attack 3 which generates 2 and can be instantly cancelled on hit while still retaining its full damage, Forte, and Concerto generation. This is a key concept used in all of Shorekeeper's best rotations.

Her Skill is also a great source of Concerto Energy. As long as it's not instantly interrupted, it'll summon some butterflies that can generate Concerto very quickly. The Forte Heavy Attack has the same effect, so to optimize rotation time, we can have the summoned butterflies hit during her Ultimate animation right before her Outro for maximum time saves.

Finally, let's talk about Shorekeeper's Intro skill, which she has two of - a standard one and an empowered one accessible only if the highest tier Stellarealm is active. The standard Intro will generally never be used as you want Shorekeeper to cast her Outro first in her rotation, and you shouldn't switch her back in once that's done and her Ultimate is cast, until your 2 other characters have done their full rotations.

However, her enhanced Intro is a key component of her Concerto generation in every rotation after her first, it deals a good amount of damage as it'll always CRIT, and it scales off her HP (like her healing does). So you'll always want to make use of it when it's the right time to switch back to Shorekeeper. It's a decent burst of damage, healing, and most importantly, it gives a high amount of Concerto (20/100). In this logic, having a weapon that helps with Concerto generation, like her Signature or Variation, is particularly helpful to speed up her rotations even more.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: We'll put it as bluntly as we can: Shorekeeper is the ONLY character from the 1.x versions that managed to survive powercreep. It's expected for Support characters to outlast DPS ones, however in the case of Shorekeeper, she is still receiving new teams to play in today. Some modern teams that feature her as the best Support you can use include Augusta, Sigrika and Jingran. She's also close to the best possible choices in Galbrena and Phrolova teams, and the best possible choice for a lot of the old teams in the game that didn't belong in niches that other specialized Supports cover, like Mornye for Tune Rupture/Strain/Mono Fusion and Chisa/Suisui for Negative Status.

Those limited Supports are her main competition, while Verina is Shorekeeper's alternative that's really easy to come by as she's a permanent banner character. However, Shorekeeper still pulls her own weight as one of the best limited banner pulls for most players' accounts to this day. Sigrika is a meta powerhouse that destroys both Tower of Adversity and Whimpering Wastes, and Jingran is one of the latest DPS releases that has firepower equal to that of the rest of the current meta. And that's with a character who's 2 years old in his team.

In conclusion, Shorekeeper's main drawbacks, not belonging to any specialized meta niches, having Verina as an easy alternative, and really wanting a Concerto weapon for her rotation speed to be optimized, are not that important compared to how much value she can provide to your account, provided you have teams that can build around her. Whenever a DPS character doesn't belong in a niche explicitly covered by a specialized Support, you can rest assured Shorekeeper will be your go-to premium Support choice. Still receiving new teams in recent times, Shorekeeper is without a doubt the longest-lasting character we've had in the Wuthering Waves meta, and it doesn't look like she'll completely fade away any time soon, even as more specialized Supports for more specialized meta niches release.
